tasks.short: Help managers and employees resolve questions, contract issues and problems at our three sites.

today.trigger: An employee or manager raises a question, disagreement or contract issue, often during a shift.
steps: Hear the employee and manager separately and establish the facts.
Find the relevant AFAS contract, applicable CAO and current SharePoint policy.
Check interpretations with Payroll, HR Administration or legal support when needed.
Discuss options with the people involved and agree an appropriate response.
Record the outcome and follow up on agreed actions.
drudgery: Searching several places for the contract and current policy.
Reconstructing an email history.
Writing repeated explanations and chasing follow-up actions.
today.time_sinks: Preparation and documentation consume time around conversations; arranging discussions across shifts also delays resolution.

lenses.faster: Prepare a brief with the contract facts, dated policy clauses, outstanding questions and a draft response. Repeated searching and rewriting disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A new restricted case entry starts document retrieval and deadline reminders. The system prepares material but waits for my approval before communicating a substantive response.
lenses.ambitious: Offer accessible HR contact hours for every shift and follow up consistently after difficult cases. Review recurring problems across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo before they become disputes.
lenses.joy: Remove email reconstruction and reminder chasing. Keep listening, mediation and helping people reach a workable agreement.
lenses.options: Compare several responses, showing contractual limits, employee impact and operational consequences. Use these to prepare for the conversation rather than select a winner automatically.
lenses.altitude: I define case handling standards, escalation routes and acceptable evidence, then improve them using recurring issues.
reach: HR Administrator: prepare routine case records and action tracking.
Payroll Specialist: assemble facts for disputed allowances without deciding payroll treatment.
HR Director: identify recurring employee relations issues for policy review.

tasks.human_edge: People need someone who listens, understands local relationships and accepts responsibility for a fair outcome. Mediation and consequential contract decisions stay with the HRBP.
tasks.pattern_why: The model helps retrieve, organise and draft; the HRBP leads the conversations and judges conflicting accounts. Deterministic reminders support the work.

in_practice.trigger: The HRBP records a new case in a proposed restricted SharePoint case list.
steps: Check access rights and retrieve only relevant AFAS facts and approved policy versions.
Prepare a source-linked brief that separates established facts, reported accounts and missing information.
Flag contractual ambiguity, urgent deadlines and issues requiring specialist review.
Let the HRBP hear the parties, assess options and approve the response.
Record the approved outcome and create reminders for agreed actions.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP checks the brief and approves every substantive response, agreement and official case record; serious matters receive appropriate specialist review.
systems: AFAS Profit through authorised reads or exports
SharePoint restricted case list and policy library
data_needed: Applicable contract and CAO, including effective dates
Approved policies and contract templates
Relevant case correspondence selected by the HRBP
Case owner, deadlines and agreed actions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint case history with source versions, approvals and action completion; official employment changes remain in AFAS.

evidence.claim: Power Automate supports approval workflows triggered by SharePoint entries, with decisions recorded in the workflow.
Source-linked case preparation can reduce searching and drafting, but mediation remains human work.
The 30% effort saving and 1.2x end-to-end speedup are untested planning estimates for Noordhaven.

risks: A summary can omit an important qualification or present an allegation as an established fact.
Selecting the wrong CAO, contract version or effective date can change an employee's entitlement.
Broad mailbox access could expose unrelated complaints or sensitive personal information.

For absence cases, keep diagnoses and medical narratives outside the HR assistant; employer records must follow the AP's restrictions. [AP guidance](https://autoriteitpersoonsgegevens.nl/themas/werk-en-uitkering/zieke-werknemers/regels-voor-werkgevers-bij-zieke-werknemers)

Wet verbetering poortwachter reminders support case management; they do not replace the bedrijfsarts or the employer and employee's reintegration discussions. [UWV guidance](https://www.uwv.nl/nl/ziek/loondoorbetaling/plan-van-aanpak)
research_questions: Across a sample of recent cases, how much time went into preparation and recording versus conversations and waiting?
Can every sampled contract question be linked to the correct CAO and policy version without manual reconstruction?
Do checked briefs preserve disputed facts and important qualifications accurately enough to save review time?
Can warehouse employees on every shift reach a human HRBP without needing a personal Microsoft 365 account?

tasks.short: Explain which HR rules apply to an employee, manager or flex worker.

today.trigger: Someone asks about leave, allowances, contracts, absence procedures or another HR rule.
steps: Clarify the question, employment arrangement and relevant date.
Identify the applicable CAO, contract and company policy.
Look up the rule and check exceptions or conflicting provisions.
Explain the answer in plain language and refer difficult interpretations to a specialist.
Save useful explanations and flag outdated policy material.
drudgery: Answering the same routine questions repeatedly.
Finding the latest approved document.
Rewriting formal policy language into practical instructions.
today.time_sinks: Repeated lookups and explanations dominate routine enquiries; personalised entitlement questions take additional checking.

lenses.faster: Retrieve the exact approved answer and its dated source instead of searching documents and rewriting it. Prepare new interpretations as drafts for my review.
lenses.autonomous: An enquiry receives an approved answer automatically when its scope, CAO and effective date match explicit rules. Missing context, contractual ambiguity and personal entitlement decisions go to HR.
lenses.ambitious: Make reliable explanations available before, during and after shifts, in the languages employees need. Maintain one approved answer library across the three sites.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive explanations and document hunting. Keep helping people understand unusual circumstances and improving confusing policies.
lenses.options: Offer a short answer, worked example and manager checklist from the same approved interpretation. Have translations checked before they enter the answer library.
lenses.altitude: I own answer quality, source maintenance and escalation rules rather than answering every routine enquiry.
reach: HR Administrator: handle routine policy enquiries.
Payroll Specialist: explain approved allowance rules without changing payroll.
Learning and Development Specialist: maintain practical policy guidance.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP resolves ambiguity and exceptions, particularly when contracts, CAOs and individual circumstances interact. Employees retain a direct route to a person.
tasks.pattern_why: Rules select and send approved answers for bounded questions. An llm_step can classify enquiries and draft additions, but new interpretations pass through agent_with_gate review before reuse.

in_practice.trigger: An employee or manager submits a question through an approved HR channel.
steps: Collect the minimum context needed to identify the employment arrangement and applicable rule.
Classify the enquiry and match it against an approved answer with scope and effective dates.
Send the approved answer with its source, or route unmatched and consequential questions to HR.
Prepare a source-linked draft for the HRBP where an answer is missing.
Let the HRBP approve library additions and suspend affected answers when source documents change.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves reusable answers and translations before release, and reviews every exception or personalised determination affecting employment rights.
systems: SharePoint approved policy and answer library
AFAS Profit for authorised employment context
Optional Copilot Studio for restricted retrieval and drafting
data_needed: Current and historical CAO and policy versions
Approved answers, examples and translations
Employment arrangement and relevant date
Document owners, review dates and escalation rules
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint enquiry log containing the answer ID, source version, routing outcome and corrections; minimise stored question text.

evidence.claim: Copilot Studio can use SharePoint as a knowledge source and restrict returned content to the signed-in user's permissions.
A controlled answer library with explicit scope and dates can automate routine explanations; this does not establish reliable autonomous legal interpretation.
The 60% effort saving and 2x end-to-end speedup assume a large share of enquiries match approved answers and remain untested.

risks: A transport employee, warehouse employee and agency worker may require different rules; site alone cannot determine CAO coverage.
Document changes can leave approved answers outdated unless ownership and effective dates are maintained.
Incorrect translations or examples can alter the meaning of contractual provisions.
Employee access and agency worker authentication require testing; a Teams-only channel would exclude some workers.

Assess OR consent requirements for changes to personnel data arrangements and disclose interaction with an AI assistant. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/~/~/link.aspx?_id=EEE76DE075754C5EBD65A0767474EF67), [European Commission AI Act guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)
research_questions: What percentage of recent enquiries can be answered using a finite approved library without interpreting an individual entitlement?
Can the system distinguish both company CAOs and agency employment arrangements reliably?
In a held-out enquiry sample, does routing catch every materially ambiguous question and avoid any incorrect entitlement answer?
Do shift workers understand and use the proposed channels, and do existing licences support the required access?

tasks.short: Help site managers match staffing, skills and development plans to the work ahead.

today.trigger: A site faces a staffing gap, seasonal peak, organisational change or internal move.
steps: Collect demand, available staffing and skills information from site managers.
Check contracts, availability, restrictions and mandatory certificates.
Compare internal moves, development, recruitment and agency capacity.
Discuss feasibility, employee preferences and costs with managers and relevant specialists.
Agree recommendations and hand implementation to the responsible operational manager.
drudgery: Combining separate staffing and certificate lists.
Checking the same constraints repeatedly.
Reworking spreadsheets when demand or availability changes.
today.time_sinks: Incomplete availability and skills records require manager follow-up; each change creates another spreadsheet comparison.

lenses.faster: Combine staffing, availability and certificate information and check explicit constraints in software. I spend less time reconciling lists and more time assessing feasible choices.
lenses.autonomous: A change in demand, availability or certificate expiry refreshes a draft capacity view and flags gaps. Managers approve individual moves and assignments.
lenses.ambitious: Maintain a rolling capacity and skills plan across all three sites, including seasonal agency demand. Identify training needs early enough to avoid preventable shortages.
lenses.joy: Remove spreadsheet rebuilding and certificate chasing. Keep discussing development opportunities and finding arrangements that work for employees and sites.
lenses.options: Compare internal movement, overtime, agency capacity, training and hiring under the same constraints. Show cost, coverage, lead time and unresolved assumptions.
lenses.altitude: I design the workforce planning rules and review their fairness and outcomes rather than assemble every staffing comparison.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: identify certificate and training gaps.
Recruiter: prepare evidence for vacancy priorities.
FP&A Analyst: prepare staffing cost scenarios for joint review.
Site workforce planner: prepare capacity comparisons while operations retains scheduling authority.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP and managers understand employee preferences, development potential and team relationships. They negotiate and approve changes affecting people.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic software checks objective constraints and calculates scenarios; the HRBP leads the judgement. The model may explain scenarios but does not rank workers by inferred personality or performance.

in_practice.trigger: A manager submits an updated demand plan or a validated staffing input changes.
steps: Read authorised AFAS and Studytube data and approved manager availability and demand files.
Flag missing or stale inputs and check certificate requirements, contractual limits and applicable working-time rules.
Calculate feasible coverage and cost scenarios using explicit, reviewable rules.
Have the HRBP and managers discuss employee preferences and operational feasibility.
Approve the chosen plan and hand actions to operations, Recruitment or Learning and Development.
in_practice.human_gate: Managers verify current availability and approve assignments; the HRBP reviews fairness and contractual implications, and Finance validates cost assumptions.
systems: AFAS Profit authorised extracts or GetConnectors
data_needed: Demand by site, period and required skill
Validated availability, contract hours and relevant assignment constraints
Required certificates and their expiry dates
Employee preferences collected for the planning purpose
Approved labour cost and agency rate assumptions
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint planning history with input timestamps, rule versions, scenarios, approvals and reasons for overrides.

evidence.claim: AFAS GetConnectors can retrieve configured Profit records through REST after App Connector and token setup.
Explicit skills, availability and contractual constraints can be checked using ordinary software; Noordhaven's proposed planning integration still needs building.
The 30% effort saving and 1.2x end-to-end speedup depend on usable demand and availability data.

risks: The supplied systems do not establish a reliable source for live rosters, availability or operational demand.
The nightly Power BI extract is too old for some immediate staffing decisions.
Course completion does not by itself prove valid certification or practical competence.
A rule can still create unfair outcomes; review allocation patterns and provide an employee challenge route.

AI allocation based on individual traits or behaviour can fall within the AI Act's high-risk employment category; a human approval step does not automatically remove that classification. [AI Act Annex III](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-3)
Check OR rights before changing working-time or personnel monitoring arrangements. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/~/~/link.aspx?_id=EEE76DE075754C5EBD65A0767474EF67)
research_questions: Where are reliable demand, roster and availability data maintained, and how quickly can they be updated?
Can explicit rules reproduce feasible options for past staffing gaps without hidden manager knowledge?
Are certificate expiry, agency capacity and cost records complete enough to compare alternatives?
Do a pilot's recommendations improve coverage and employee outcomes after counting data correction and review effort?

tasks.short: Advise site managers on hiring and retention programmes that produce successful hires at day 90.

today.trigger: Hiring slows, early departures increase, or a manager requests a recruiting or retention programme.
steps: Gather recruitment, onboarding, retention and manager feedback for the affected roles and sites.
Check definitions and compare cohorts, shifts and employment arrangements.
Discuss likely causes with recruiters, managers and recent hires.
Develop programme options, costs, responsibilities and success measures.
Recommend an approach and review results after implementation.
drudgery: Joining recruitment and employee records.
Recalculating the same cohort measures.
Turning scattered notes into programme proposals.
today.time_sinks: Data joins, missing onboarding evidence and inconsistent definitions delay advice; proving whether a programme helped takes longer.

lenses.faster: Prepare consistent cohort measures and a source-linked account of where hiring and onboarding break down. Draft the programme brief from checked findings.
lenses.autonomous: A scheduled refresh flags agreed changes in time to hire, acceptance, week-one onboarding and day-90 outcomes. It prepares a review brief rather than deciding what caused the change.
lenses.ambitious: Run small, measured improvements for each site's main hiring problems and learn across sites. Optimise for productive hires who remain after 90 days, not simply fast vacancy closure.
lenses.joy: Remove recurring data assembly and slide preparation. Keep discussing causes with people and designing practical improvements.
lenses.options: Compare buddy support, manager check-ins, realistic job previews, onboarding changes and recruiting channel changes. Show cost, expected mechanism and how each option would be evaluated.
lenses.altitude: I manage a portfolio of hiring and retention experiments and stop programmes that do not improve the North Star.
reach: Recruiter: diagnose pipeline bottlenecks and propose programme changes.
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: frame cohort questions and interpret checked results.
Learning and Development Specialist: design onboarding interventions.
FP&A Analyst: prepare programme cost and benefit assumptions.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP distinguishes a plausible story from a supported explanation and secures manager commitment. Employees' experiences and operational context determine which intervention is worth trying.
tasks.pattern_why: Software calculates agreed metrics and the model drafts hypotheses and options. Humans determine causality, choose interventions and approve changes.

in_practice.trigger: The monthly review date arrives or an agreed programme metric crosses a review threshold.
steps: Join authorised Recruitee, AFAS and onboarding data using verified identifiers and freeze the reporting period.
Calculate agreed metrics, showing unfilled vacancies, missing evidence and hires not yet at day 90 separately.
Prepare a brief with observed changes, alternative explanations and programme options.
Have the HRBP test the findings with recruiters, managers and employee feedback.
Approve a pilot with an owner, budget, comparison method and review date.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst validates joins and measures; the HRBP approves recommendations, managers own delivery, and the HR Director approves material policy or budget changes.
systems: Recruitee authorised exports or API reads
data_needed: Vacancy dates, pipeline stages, offers and accepted hires
Start dates and employment status at day 90
Week-one onboarding evidence
An agreed, human-validated definition of productive at day 90
Relevant shift, site, role, programme exposure and cost information
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint programme register with metric definitions, data snapshots, hypotheses, approvals and pilot outcomes.

evidence.claim: Power BI supports scheduled data refresh, providing a basis for recurring metric preparation when source connectivity is configured.
Combining checked cohort analysis with drafted options can accelerate programme preparation; it does not establish causal effects.
The 40% effort saving and 1.3x preparation-to-decision speedup are untested; observing day-90 outcomes still takes 90 days.

risks: Counting only hires would turn the North Star into a retention measure and hide unfilled roles; freeze the vacancy cohort and evaluation window.
Productivity evidence is not established in the supplied systems and needs an agreed operational assessment.
Seasonality, agency mix and manager changes can explain apparent programme effects.
Individual flight-risk scores could encourage intrusive or discriminatory treatment; use group analysis and employee conversations.
Assess AI Act classification if the design expands into candidate evaluation or targeted job advertising. [AI Act Annex III](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-3)
Programme changes to recruitment or training policies can require OR consent. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/~/~/link.aspx?_id=EEE76DE075754C5EBD65A0767474EF67)
research_questions: Can Recruitee vacancies and hires be joined reliably to AFAS employees without importing unnecessary candidate data?
Who can validate productive-at-day-90 outcomes, and how much evidence is currently missing?
Which programme choices would managers change after seeing the proposed brief?
Can a phased or comparable-cohort pilot distinguish programme effects from seasonality and staffing mix?

tasks.short: Help managers interview fairly, discuss performance and document problems properly.

today.trigger: A manager prepares an interview, appraisal or difficult performance conversation, or needs training.
steps: Clarify the manager's situation and the skills they need.
Retrieve approved interview, appraisal and performance documentation guidance.
Prepare examples, checklists or a short training session.
Coach the manager and practise difficult conversations.
Check follow-up documentation and arrange further support where needed.
drudgery: Rebuilding similar training material.
Finding appropriate examples and templates.
Correcting vague or incomplete documentation.
today.time_sinks: Preparing tailored materials and checking records takes time; scheduling coaching around shifts limits reach.

lenses.faster: Draft a tailored checklist and practice scenario from approved guidance. Check documentation for missing dates, examples and agreed follow-up without inventing facts.
lenses.autonomous: An approved manager learning assignment triggers preparation of the relevant material and practice exercises. Completion reminders run automatically; the HRBP reviews substantive guidance.
lenses.ambitious: Give every shift supervisor short, repeated practice rather than relying on occasional classroom training. Check whether managers apply the skills in interviews, onboarding and feedback.
lenses.joy: Remove slide rebuilding and template correction. Keep live coaching and helping managers improve difficult conversations.
lenses.options: Practise several interview and feedback situations using fictional employees. Compare ways to ask clear questions and explain expectations fairly.
lenses.altitude: I design a manager coaching system and improve it using observed needs and checked outcomes.
reach: Learning and Development Specialist: prepare manager learning modules and exercises.
Recruiter: create structured interview guides.
HR Administrator: improve completeness of approved documentation templates.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP models respectful behaviour and challenges unfair assumptions. Real performance judgements and consequential employee conversations require accountable people.
tasks.pattern_why: The model drafts materials and plays fictional practice roles while the HRBP remains the coach. Rule-based checks flag missing documentation fields.

in_practice.trigger: A manager requests support or receives an approved Studytube learning assignment.
steps: Select approved guidance and the manager's stated learning need.
Draft a checklist, short lesson and fictional practice scenarios.
Have the HRBP check accuracy, fairness and alignment with Noordhaven's procedures.
Let the manager practise and receive coaching against approved criteria.
Record learning completion and agreed follow-up; verify real case documentation separately.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP approves training content and handles real employee cases; managers verify every factual statement in their documentation.
data_needed: Approved interviewing, appraisal and documentation standards
Role requirements and structured interview criteria
Fictional practice scenarios
Manager learning assignments and completion records
Minimal real case facts only when separately authorised for review
in_practice.logs_to: Studytube learning records and restricted SharePoint content approvals; keep fictional practice separate from employee and candidate files.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft training material and conduct fictional conversation practice with human review.
Explicit documentation requirements can be checked in software without using a model to judge employee performance.
The 40% effort saving and 1.3x preparation-and-delivery speedup are untested estimates; manager skill improvement needs separate measurement.

risks: Generated guidance can suggest inappropriate interview questions or an unfair performance process.
Fluent wording can conceal invented incidents, quotations or dates; the assistant must flag missing facts.
Training completion and convincing role-play do not prove a manager can handle a real conversation well.

Do not infer emotions from managers' or employees' voices or faces; workplace emotion recognition is generally prohibited by the AI Act, subject to narrow exceptions. [European Commission guidance](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)
Using AI to evaluate real candidates or employees requires a separate classification and governance assessment. [AI Act Annex III](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-3)
Changes to personnel training or appraisal arrangements can require OR consent. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/~/~/link.aspx?_id=EEE76DE075754C5EBD65A0767474EF67)
research_questions: Which recurring manager requests consume the most HRBP preparation time?
Can approved materials support realistic scenarios for warehouse, transport and office managers without exposing real cases?
Does a pilot improve observed interview and documentation quality compared with current coaching?
Do preparation and review savings remain after counting content corrections and manager support?

tasks.short: Design ways to hear employee concerns and measure satisfaction across sites and shifts.

today.trigger: A policy changes, working conditions cause concern, or HR reviews satisfaction and complaint procedures.
steps: Discuss objectives and trust concerns with employees, managers and the OR.
Review existing questions, complaint routes and accessibility across shifts.
Design questions, sampling, confidentiality arrangements and escalation procedures.
Agree ownership, privacy safeguards and required OR involvement.
Pilot the approach and revise it before wider use.
drudgery: Rewriting survey questions and procedure drafts.
Comparing versions and documenting consultation comments.
Checking whether every site and shift is covered.
today.time_sinks: Method design, privacy decisions and consultation take time; poorly designed questions can create unusable results.

lenses.faster: Draft questionnaire and procedure alternatives and check wording, accessibility and coverage. Consultation and testing stay with me.
lenses.autonomous: Once approved, schedules can start feedback rounds and track agreed follow-up dates. Formal complaints enter a separate restricted human handling route.
lenses.ambitious: Hear warehouse and transport shifts as consistently as office staff, and include agency workers through agreed arrangements. Close the loop by telling employees what changed because of their feedback.
lenses.joy: Remove repetitive drafting, version comparison and coverage checks. Keep listening, building trust and designing a process people will use.
lenses.options: Compare a short pulse, structured interviews, shift discussions and a fuller survey. Show the trade-offs in access, burden, comparability and confidentiality.
lenses.altitude: I design and maintain a trustworthy listening and complaint system, then check whether employees can safely use it.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: specify sampling and reporting safeguards.
HR Director: prepare complaint procedure and OR consultation proposals.
Site managers: design accessible shift feedback arrangements.

tasks.human_edge: Employees and the OR help determine whether confidentiality promises are credible. The HRBP judges fairness, hears difficult concerns and ensures complaints receive appropriate human attention.
tasks.pattern_why: AI supports method drafting and comparison; humans design confidentiality, escalation and consultation. The task concerns the method, not automated complaint adjudication.

in_practice.trigger: The HR Director requests a new listening method or a review of the complaint procedure.
steps: Map employee groups, shift access, existing complaint routes and the intended decisions.
Draft alternative methods, plain-language questions and confidentiality explanations.
Have employees, the OR and privacy support review the proposed approach.
Pilot comprehension, access and confidentiality safeguards with representative groups.
Approve the method, owners and escalation routes before scheduling broader use.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP and HR Director approve the design with privacy review and required OR consent; complaints are assigned to accountable human handlers.
systems: SharePoint controlled method and procedure library
Excel for sampling and pilot analysis
Optional Microsoft Forms or another approved survey tool
data_needed: Group counts by site, shift and employment arrangement
Existing complaint and escalation procedures
Survey questions, consultation comments and pilot results
Retention periods, access rules and reporting suppression rules
Agency arrangements for worker participation
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint design and approval history; raw feedback and complaints use separate restricted stores with defined retention.

evidence.claim: Language models can draft and compare survey questions and procedure options, but cannot establish their validity or employee trust.
Approved schedules and review tasks can use ordinary workflow automation; Noordhaven's listening design remains a proposal.
The 35% effort saving and 1.25x design-cycle speedup are untested and apply to method design rather than report production.

risks: A survey can exclude workers without convenient digital access or sufficient language support.
Anonymous feedback may still identify people through small groups, detailed comments or linked metadata.
A proposed minimum reporting group of 10 is only a starting rule; complementary suppression and comment redaction also need testing.
Survey channels must clearly distinguish feedback from urgent safety reports, grievances and whistleblowing routes.
Complaint, privacy and personnel monitoring arrangements can require OR consent. [SER guidance](https://www.ser.nl/nl/thema/medezeggenschap/~/~/link.aspx?_id=EEE76DE075754C5EBD65A0767474EF67)
Collecting more data than needed or reusing feedback for individual performance decisions would undermine the stated purpose and AVG/GDPR safeguards.
research_questions: Which site, shift, language and agency groups are currently underrepresented, and what channels would reach them?
Do pilot participants understand the questions and the limits of confidentiality?
Can reporting and comment handling prevent identification in realistic small-group examples?
Will the OR and employees support the design, and can designated handlers meet its complaint response commitments?

tasks.short: Prepare a checked management report on employee satisfaction and agreed follow-up actions.

today.trigger: A feedback round finishes or management requests an employee satisfaction presentation.
steps: Collect feedback results and relevant HR measures for the agreed period.
Check totals, response coverage and confidentiality.
Calculate comparisons and manually group comments into themes.
Prepare charts, a narrative and proposed follow-up actions.
Present the findings and record management decisions.
drudgery: Cleaning exports and recalculating charts.
Grouping similar comments.
Copying results into slides and checking figures again.
today.time_sinks: Cleaning, chart preparation and narrative drafting dominate production; checking anonymity and explaining results still require judgement.

lenses.faster: Calculate approved measures and generate charts from a validated snapshot. Draft the narrative from checked tables and privacy-screened themes.
lenses.autonomous: A completed feedback round starts validation and prepares a report for approval. Failed checks stop production and create an exception for the owner.
lenses.ambitious: Provide consistent reports and action reviews for all sites, with safe comparisons across shifts. Show whether agreed improvements were completed and what changed afterward.
lenses.joy: Remove copying numbers, rebuilding charts and formatting repeated slides. Keep interpreting difficult findings and discussing action with managers.
lenses.options: Prepare a short management brief, an OR version and a site discussion pack from the same checked evidence. Vary detail and permissions while keeping the figures consistent.
lenses.altitude: I own reporting definitions, review quality and action follow-through rather than assemble every report.
reach: People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: produce standard descriptive reporting under shared definitions.
HR Director: prepare management and OR reporting packs.
Site managers: maintain evidence and follow-up for agreed employee experience actions.

tasks.human_edge: The HRBP explains uncertainty, challenges selective interpretations and turns findings into realistic actions. Sensitive results require thoughtful discussion with employees and managers.
tasks.pattern_why: Deterministic software validates and calculates; an llm_step drafts comment themes and narrative. A multi-step workflow prepares the pack, and the HRBP approves it before release.

in_practice.trigger: The feedback owner closes a reporting period and confirms that the required source refresh succeeded.
steps: Freeze the source snapshot and validate totals, response coverage and reporting definitions.
Apply small-group and complementary suppression, and screen comments for identifying details.
Calculate metrics and render approved report pages; give the model only checked tables and screened comments.
Draft a narrative that separates observations, uncertainty and proposed actions.
Have the HRBP approve the pack, then record its release and action owners.
in_practice.human_gate: The HRBP verifies figures, confidentiality, themes and wording before each release; the analyst reviews data exceptions and changed measures.
systems: Proposed workflow and approved LLM service
data_needed: Approved feedback results and screened comments
Population and response counts
Metric definitions, comparison periods and suppression rules
Source refresh timestamps
Previously agreed actions, owners and status
in_practice.logs_to: Restricted SharePoint report history with snapshot ID, validation results, suppressed outputs, reviewer approval and action register.

evidence.claim: Power BI can export report pages to PowerPoint as static images with links back to the report.
A model can draft themes and narrative from checked inputs, but human review is needed for omissions and unsupported explanations.
The 70% effort saving and 2.5x end-to-end report-production speedup are untested; unattended export depends on the chosen implementation and licences.

risks: Low or uneven response rates can make site comparisons misleading.
Suppressed values may be reconstructed from totals or other report versions.
Comment summaries can miss minority concerns or reveal identities through quotations.
Generated narrative can present correlation as causation or overstate small changes.
Static PowerPoint exports can circulate beyond intended viewers; distribution controls must accompany report permissions.
A failed nightly refresh or unvalidated survey import can produce a polished report from stale data.
research_questions: Can the workflow reproduce a previous approved report with matching totals and suppression decisions?
How much production time remains after counting validation, narrative corrections and approval?
Can realistic attempts to combine report views or comments identify individuals?
Do managers and the OR understand uncertainty and agree actions more readily from the proposed pack?

role.altitude: The HRBP becomes the owner of fair employee relations, reliable HR guidance and measurable workforce improvements across the three sites. Routine preparation moves into controlled workflows, leaving more time for employee conversations, manager coaching and programme decisions.
reach: HR Administration: routine enquiry handling, case preparation and follow-up design.
People Analytics and HRIS: define workforce questions, interpret validated cohorts and review reporting quality.
Recruitment: prioritise hiring improvements against productive, retained day-90 outcomes.
Learning and Development: design manager coaching and onboarding improvements.
FP&A and site planning: prepare workforce scenarios with validated cost and operational assumptions.
HR Director: prepare policy proposals and evidence for OR consultation, while the Director retains decision authority.
role.ceiling_note: Today's workflows and time anatomy are inferred from the fictional company brief. The listed tasks cover 798.4 hours per FTE yearly, about half of the role. The estimates imply 335.8 hours of gross annual capacity per FTE, or 1,007.4 hours across three HRBPs, valued at about EUR 80,590 at EUR 80/hour before implementation and running costs; this is capacity, not cash savings or a staffing reduction. Time_saved_pct measures HRBP effort; speedup estimates elapsed task completion including automated steps and human review, with smaller gains where meetings or consultation dominate. Shared preparation is counted once, method design is separate from reporting, and nothing is extrapolated to unlisted work. Trust, specialist judgement, operational data quality, OR processes and actual employee outcomes limit expansion. Proposed AI and workflow products require licence, access and integration checks.
skills_to_grow: Maintain approved interpretations with CAO coverage, source versions and effective dates.
Design clear workflow rules, exceptions, approvals and audit records.
Validate data joins, denominators, cohort maturity and productivity evidence.
Evaluate pilots without confusing seasonal changes with programme effects.
Apply AVG/GDPR purpose limits, access controls, retention and confidentiality safeguards.
